metadata.dataset_description: The dataset consists of 500 entries simulating ServiceNow fm_expense_line table, which records various attributes of financial expenses. Key fields include 'number', 'opened_at', 'amount', 'state', 'short_description', 'ci', 'user', 'department', 'category', 'process_date', 'source_id', and 'type'. This table documents the flow of financial transactions by detailing the amount, departmental allocation, and the nature of each expense. Provides a clear view of organizational expenditures across different categories, highlighting both the timing and the approval state of each financial entry.
metadata.goal: To identify and rectify the causes of high rejection rates in travel expenses to ensure that submissions  align with organizational policies.

predicted_insights: While IT has the highest decline rate, Customer Support contributes the majority of Travel declines (35 of 61, ≈57%), suggesting the biggest absolute reduction opportunity lies in improving Customer Support submissions, alongside addressing IT’s policy-alignment issues.
Within Travel submissions missing source_id, declines are the most common outcome, exceeding processed by 9 cases (61 vs 52), meaning such submissions are more likely to be declined than processed.

Smaller and mid-sized Travel expenses are rejected substantially more often than the largest ones—Q1’s decline rate is ~1.5× Q4’s—indicating that targeting guidance and checks on low-to-mid ticket claims could yield the biggest reduction in rejections.

Despite "asset" appearing in about 64% of Travel submissions, their decline rate is 3.81 percentage points lower (≈9% relatively) than non-asset entries, suggesting rejections are driven more by non-asset-related factors.

Across Jun-2023 to Apr-2024, the Travel decline rate averaged about 41.7% (median 42.86%), with 7 of 11 months at or above 40%, indicating persistently high rejections; the sharp fall from 53.85% in Mar-2024 to 27.27% in Apr-2024 suggests a recent improvement worth investigating.

Across the top 30 declined Travel expense descriptions, 28 of 30 explicitly mention “asset,” “equipment,” or “hardware,” and the top three descriptions alone account for 10 of 37 instances (27%), suggesting many rejections stem from asset/equipment-related submissions misclassified as Travel.
Nearly 2 in 5 Travel expenses lacking a source_id are declined (61/146 ≈ 41.8%), suggesting that ensuring source_id is captured could meaningfully lower rejection rates.

The inability to compute a Declined median for Travel (amid 205 of 500 records overall lacking processed_date, i.e., ~41%) highlights a data capture gap that prevents benchmarking rejection turnaround, whereas Processed Travel items move through in about 2.3 days median.
A 41.78% decline rate for Travel submissions lacking a source_id suggests that ensuring this field is populated could potentially prevent roughly 2 out of every 5 declines within this subset.

The top three users (Ofelia Sheffler, Sal Pindell, Zackary Mockus) account for 10 of the 15 declines (≈66.7%) among the frequent Travel submitters listed, with a combined decline rate of 55.6% (10 declines over 18 submissions), suggesting focused guidance for a small group could materially reduce rejections.

The median Travel decline rate across departments is 40.9%, with Q1 at 0% and Q3 at 50.0%, highlighting wide variability—only Development and Product Management have zero declines, while IT and HR exceed 50%.

The 3.6% higher average for Processed versus Declined Travel expenses suggests rejection likelihood is not primarily driven by higher amounts, pointing instead to non-monetary factors (e.g., policy compliance or documentation) as likely causes.
predicted_summary:
Declines are concentrated in specific parts of the organization within Travel: IT has the highest decline rate (reported between 54.6% by department view and 75% in another slice), followed by HR at 50%, Customer Support at 44.3%, and Sales at 40.9%, while Finance is lower at 25% and Development/Product Management show 0%. At the individual level (users with ≥5 submissions), the highest decline rates include Ofelia Sheffler at 80% (4/5), Sal Pindell at 50% (3/6), Zackary Mockus at 42.86% (3/7), and Geri Forness and Lynda Caraway at 40% each (2/5).
Decline rates vary meaningfully with expense size in Travel: the lowest and mid quartiles see higher declines—Q1 at 48.65% (18/37) and Q3 at 47.22% (17/36)—while the highest quartile has the lowest decline rate at 32.43% (12/37), with Q2 at 38.89% (14/36). Despite this pattern, average amounts are similar for Declined ($3,792.89) and Processed ($3,927.87) expenses, indicating amount alone is not a strong differentiator at the mean but matters across the distribution.
Travel rejections rose in late 2023 and stayed elevated into early 2024 before dropping sharply: monthly decline rates were 40% (Jun-2023), 50% (Jul), a low of 21.43% (Sep), a peak of 57.14% (Nov), remaining around 43–54% through Mar-2024 (53.85% in Mar), then falling to 27.27% in Apr-2024. Metadata and description signals show mixed effects: submissions missing source_id have a 41.78% decline rate (61/146), and items with “asset” in the short description see slightly lower declines (40.43% vs 44.23%), yet the most frequent declined descriptions reference automated asset creation/registration.
